observation.visible_scene: A hydraulic press setup: a large steel hex nut lies on its side between two cylindrical platens wrapped in yellow-and-black hazard tape, with its threaded bore facing the camera. A polished chrome ram sits above the upper platen against a plain light-gray wall. The lower platen rests on a dark base.
visible_changes: The upper platen descends slowly and continuously throughout the excerpt, its lower edge dropping by a small but steady amount relative to the fixed lower platen.

The hex nut is progressively compressed in the vertical direction: its top face flattens against the descending platen and its overall height shrinks while the bottom stays in contact with the lower platen.
The threaded bore remains open and roughly circular, showing only slight distortion consistent with the nut being squashed; the nut's outer hexagonal silhouette bulges/shifts subtly as it deforms.
The lower platen, the dark base, and the background wall remain stationary, indicating the change is object motion (platen + nut deformation), not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the nut ultimately fails, splits, or fully collapses after this segment.
The state before the excerpt (initial gap, when contact began) and the applied force/pressure values.
The exact material grade of the nut.
uncertain_details: Precise pixel positions of the platen edges; the descent is slow and the total displacement within the crop is modest.
Whether the threaded bore's diameter changes measurably versus appearing so due to the nut's tilt/shape change.
Any microscopic surface marks or early cracks are not clearly resolvable in the frames.
